While both aim to test feasibility, a proof of concept is generally more focused on demonstrating that a specific idea or method is viable, often without actual implementation, whereas pilot testing involves executing a smaller version of the project or experiment. ### Pilot Testing vs Full-Scale Implementation. Pilot testing occurs before full-scale implementation and serves to identify potential issues in a controlled, smaller setting. Full-scale implementation is the complete rollout after successful pilot testing. The main purpose of pilot testing is to evaluate the feasibility, cost, duration, and potential risks associated with a project or experiment on a smaller scale before proceeding to full-scale implementation. ### How long should a pilot test last? ### How do you select participants for a pilot test? ### What should you do if a pilot test fails? Pilot Testing is a critical step in project management and research, serving as a preliminary assessment to gauge feasibility, cost, time, and potential risks. By conducting pilot tests, organizations and researchers can make data-driven decisions, ensuring that the full-scale projects are executed efficiently and effectively. Through careful planning, execution, and analysis, pilot testing helps to mitigate risks and optimize resources, paving the way for successful project implementations.

results.title: FDA Announces Completion of First AI-Assisted Scientific Review ...
results.content: # FDA Announces Completion of First AI-Assisted Scientific Review Pilot and Aggressive Agency-Wide AI Rollout Timeline. Makary, M.D., M.P.H., today announced an aggressive timeline to scale use of artificial intelligence (AI) internally across all FDA centers by June 30, 2025, following the completion of a new generative AI pilot for scientific reviewers. **“This is a game-changer technology that has enabled me to perform scientific review tasks in minutes that used to take three days,” said Jinzhong (Jin) Liu, Deputy Director, Office of Drug Evaluation Sciences, Office of New Drugs in FDA’s Center for Drug Evaluation and Research (CDER).**. By that date, all centers will be operating on a common, secure generative AI system integrated with FDA’s internal data platforms. The FDA, an agency within the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, protects the public health by assuring the safety, effectiveness, and security of human and veterinary drugs, vaccines and other biological products for human use, and medical devices.
